@Tanner Duve published a blogpost on writing quantum algorithms in lean :

https://tannerduve.github.io/blog/2026/quantum-algos/#GHZ
@Bas Spitters it turns out there is already a topic to discuss quantum algorithms

Context : #CSLib > Developing quantum algorithms in CSLib @ 💬

In the interest of coordinating across multiple attempts to formalize quantum algorithms, I am writing a list of groups that I am aware of, who are working on formalizing quantum computing in one form or another. For each group, I'll try to tag one person per entry to avoid spamming everyone. Hopefully we can converge on common definitions and theorem statements.

  1. David Gross's research group at Uni Köln. Their work is currently not dependent on CSLib and physlib, and some of their work on lie groups might be suitable for mathlib.
  2. @Maris Ozols and co from Amsterdam.
  3. The TU Darmstadt group (@Andrés Goens, @Marcus Rossel)
  4. @Henrik Lievonen at CISPA. Henrik works on distributed graph algorithms in lean (Shreyas4991/DGAlgorithms) and is interested in formalizing the quantum local model + algorithms. His PhD thesis provides the first formal definition of the model.
  5. In Algolean, we are building off Free monads, and Physlib's CPTP maps. @Tanner Duve is the author of the quantum models and algorithms including Deutsch Josza, which was presented as part of our poster at STOC.
  6. Bas Spitters mentions in this thread #CSLib > Developing quantum algorithms in CSLib @ 💬 that their group is working on a library of quantum algorithms.
1. Additionally @Alex Meiburg and @Markus Bläser are interested in quantum algorithms and complexity theory and Alex has their own formalizations.

My interest is in post-quantum cryptography and quantum compilers.

@Fady Adal and @Robert Rand have https://github.com/inQWIRE/LeanQuantum

Additionally here's our Algolean poster with Deutsch-Josza as an example. The poster and talk linked in there was meant for an algorithms theory audience, so PL concepts are explained in handwavy terms :

There's a question of whether one wants to depend on Physlib or not. For example a lot of work I saw in David Gross's group's repository would augment Mathlib or Physlib very well. In contrast in Algolean, our approach has been to leave the physics to physlib. There are pros and cons to both approaches.
